quiz.title: T4.1: Traverses and Sorts Arrays
quiz.description: Scenario-based questions on subscript sorting (canonical ordering), $ORDER traversal, multi-level $ORDER, $DATA existence checks, and reverse traversal in ObjectScript arrays.

questions.question:
Consider the following array:

set data("apple") = 1
set data("banana") = 2
set data(100) = 3
set data(20) = 4

What is the first subscript returned by $ORDER(data(""))?
questions.explanation: In canonical ordering, numeric subscripts come before string subscripts, and they are sorted numerically: 20 < 100. So $ORDER(data("")) returns 20 as the first subscript. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_variables#GCOS_variables_global_subscripts)

questions.question:
Consider the following array:

set y = 10
set y("X") = 11
set y("Y") = 22
set y("X", 1) = 33
set y("X", 2) = 44
set y("Y", 1) = 55
set y("Y", 2) = 66

You would like to write a loop that prints all the values in the second level, so that the output looks like this:

33445566

Which of the following code blocks accomplishes that?
questions.explanation: To traverse all second-level subscripts, you need nested $ORDER loops. The outer loop iterates over first-level subscripts ("X", "Y"), and for each, the inner loop iterates over second-level subscripts (1, 2). Option (a) only reads first-level values. Option (b) uses $QUERY incorrectly. Option (d) has syntax errors. The nested $ORDER loop correctly produces 33445566. (Reference: InterSystems Practice Q14; https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_forder)

questions.question:
A developer is loading patient records into a local array and notices the traversal order is unexpected. Consider:

set patients(3) = "Chen"
set patients("10A") = "Patel"
set patients(1) = "Smith"
set patients(10) = "Jones"
set patients("2B") = "Garcia"

What is the $ORDER traversal order of the subscripts?
questions.explanation: Canonical ordering places numeric subscripts first (sorted numerically: 1, 3, 10), then string subscripts (sorted by ASCII collation: "10A" before "2B" because "1" < "2" in ASCII). "10A" and "2B" are strings because they contain non-numeric characters. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_variables#GCOS_variables_global_subscripts)

questions.question:
You are debugging a routine that checks whether a global node has children. Consider:

set ^inventory("warehouse") = "Main"
set ^inventory("warehouse", "aisle1") = 50
set ^inventory("warehouse", "aisle2") = 30

write $DATA(^inventory("warehouse"))

What is the output?
questions.explanation: $DATA returns 11 when a node has both a value AND descendant nodes. ^inventory("warehouse") has the value "Main" and also has child subscripts ("aisle1" and "aisle2"), so $DATA returns 11. Return values: 0=undefined, 1=value only, 10=descendants only, 11=both. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fdata)

questions.question:
A colleague asks you to review their array traversal code. Consider:

set arr(1) = "A"
set arr(3) = "B"
set arr(10) = "C"
set arr(2) = "D"
set key = ""
for {
  set key = $ORDER(arr(key))
  quit:key=""
  write arr(key)
}

What is the output?
questions.explanation: $ORDER traverses numeric subscripts in numeric order: 1, 2, 3, 10. So the output is arr(1)="A", arr(2)="D", arr(3)="B", arr(10)="C" = "ADBC". The insertion order does not matter; canonical ordering always applies. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_forder)

questions.question:
You need to find the last item in a price list stored in a global. Consider:

set ^prices(10) = 9.99
set ^prices(20) = 14.99
set ^prices(30) = 24.99
set ^prices(40) = 39.99

Which code correctly retrieves the last subscript (40)?
questions.explanation: $ORDER with direction -1 starting from "" returns the last subscript in the array. $ORDER(^prices(""), -1) returns 40. Starting from "" with direction 1 gives the first subscript; starting from "" with direction -1 gives the last. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_forder)

questions.question:
You are writing a utility that retrieves both the key and value in a single $ORDER call. Consider:

set scores("Alice") = 95
set scores("Bob") = 87
set scores("Carol") = 92

set key = ""
set key = $ORDER(scores(key), 1, val)
write key, ": ", val

What is the output?
questions.explanation: The third argument of $ORDER receives the data value at the next node. Starting from "", the first subscript in canonical order is "Alice" (A < B < C in ASCII). The value 95 is stored in val. Output: "Alice: 95". (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_forder)

questions.question:
While investigating a bug, you examine an array that uses negative subscripts:

set arr(-3) = "X"
set arr(0) = "Y"
set arr(2) = "Z"
set arr(-1) = "W"
set key = ""
for {
  set key = $ORDER(arr(key))
  quit:key=""
  write key, " "
}

What is the output?
questions.explanation: Numeric subscripts are sorted in numeric order, including negative numbers. The traversal order is -3, -1, 0, 2. Canonical numeric sorting respects the actual numeric value. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_variables#GCOS_variables_global_subscripts)

questions.question: Which of the following are valid return values of the $DATA function? (Select all that apply)
options: 1 - node has a value, no descendants
10 - no value at this node, but has descendants
11 - node has a value AND has descendants
100 - node has descendants at multiple levels
questions.explanation: $DATA returns only four possible values: 0, 1, 10, 11. The tens digit indicates descendants (0=none, 1=has descendants), and the ones digit indicates a value (0=none, 1=has value). Values like 5 and 100 are never returned. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fdata)

questions.question:
A developer sets up a configuration array and is confused by the sorting. Consider:

set cfg("abc") = 1
set cfg("ABC") = 2
set cfg("Abc") = 3
set key = ""
for {
  set key = $ORDER(cfg(key))
  quit:key=""
  write cfg(key)
}

What is the output?
questions.explanation: String subscripts are sorted in ASCII order. In ASCII, uppercase letters come before lowercase: 'A'=65, 'a'=97. So "ABC" (all uppercase) < "Abc" (A then lowercase) < "abc" (all lowercase). Output: cfg("ABC")=2, cfg("Abc")=3, cfg("abc")=1 = "231". (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_variables#GCOS_variables_global_subscripts)

questions.question:
You are building an order processing routine. Consider the following code:

set orders(1001,"item") = "Widget"
set orders(1001,"qty") = 5
set orders(1002,"item") = "Gadget"
set orders(1002,"qty") = 3

set key = ""
for {
  set key = $ORDER(orders(key))
  quit:key=""
  write "Order: ", ordKey, !
  write "  Item: ", orders(key,"item"), !
}

What happens when this code runs?
options: <UNDEFINED> error because ordKey was never set
<SUBSCRIPT> error because nested subscripts cannot be traversed
questions.explanation: The loop uses the variable ordKey in the Write statement, but ordKey was never assigned a value. The correct variable should be key (which is set by $ORDER). This is a common typo bug that causes an <UNDEFINED> *ordKey error at runtime. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RERR_gen#RERR_UNDEFINED)

questions.question:
A reporting module stores data in a deep hierarchy. Consider:

set ^data("a","b","c") = "deep"
write $DATA(^data("a","b"))

What is the output?
questions.explanation: ^data("a","b") was never explicitly assigned a value, but it has a descendant node at ("a","b","c"). Therefore $DATA returns 10: no value at this node, but descendants exist. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fdata)

questions.question:
You need to process decimal product IDs. Consider:

set arr(1.5) = "A"
set arr(1) = "B"
set arr(2) = "C"
set arr(1.10) = "D"
set key = ""
for {
  set key = $ORDER(arr(key))
  quit:key=""
  write arr(key)
}

What is the output?
questions.explanation: Numeric subscripts are sorted by numeric value. 1.10 is canonically equivalent to 1.1. The sort order is: 1, 1.1, 1.5, 2. So: arr(1)="B", arr(1.1)="D", arr(1.5)="A", arr(2)="C" = "BDAC". Trailing zeros are stripped in canonical form. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_variables#GCOS_variables_global_subscripts)

questions.question:
You are verifying that a configuration node was properly cleaned up. Consider:

kill ^config("db")
set ^config("db","host") = "localhost"
set ^config("db","port") = 1972

write $DATA(^config("db"))

What is the output?
questions.explanation: After KILL ^config("db"), the node and all descendants are removed. Then two child nodes are created under ^config("db"), but ^config("db") itself is never given a value. So $DATA returns 10: no value, but has descendants. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fdata)

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

kill arr
set arr(1) = "one"
set arr(2) = "two"
set key = ""
set key = $ORDER(arr(key))
set key = $ORDER(arr(key))
set key = $ORDER(arr(key))
write key
questions.explanation: Starting from "", the first $ORDER returns 1, the second returns 2, and the third call (from subscript 2) returns "" because there are no more subscripts. So key is "" and Write outputs an empty string. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_forder)

questions.question: A junior developer asks about $ORDER behavior. Which of the following statements are true? (Select all that apply)
options: $ORDER with direction -1 traverses subscripts in reverse order
$ORDER returns "" when there are no more subscripts at that level
$ORDER can accept a third argument to retrieve the node's data value
$ORDER can only be used with global arrays, not local arrays
questions.explanation: $ORDER traverses subscripts at a single level only - it does NOT automatically descend into child subscripts (use nested $ORDER or $QUERY for that). It works with both local and global arrays. Direction -1 enables reverse traversal, it returns "" at the end, and the optional third argument retrieves the node value. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_forder)

questions.question:
You want to safely check whether a global node exists before reading it. Which approach avoids an <UNDEFINED> error?

set value = ^settings("timeout")
questions.explanation: Only $GET safely avoids <UNDEFINED> in all cases. While $DATA(^settings("timeout")) returns a truthy value (10) when the node has subnodes but no value at the node itself, the subsequent SET still causes <UNDEFINED> because the node has no data. The correct $DATA check would be $DATA(...)#2 (bitwise AND with 2) to verify the node has a value. $GET(^settings("timeout"),30) safely returns the default value 30 when the node has no value, regardless of subnodes. $ORDER returns the next subscript, not the value. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fget)

questions.question:
You are building an index of error codes. Consider:

set ^errors(100) = "Timeout"
set ^errors(200) = "Not Found"
set ^errors("AUTH01") = "Unauthorized"
set ^errors("AUTH02") = "Forbidden"
set ^errors(500) = "Internal"

set key = ""
set key = $ORDER(^errors(key))
set key = $ORDER(^errors(key))
set key = $ORDER(^errors(key))
write ^errors(key)
questions.explanation: Canonical ordering: numeric subscripts come first sorted numerically (100, 200, 500), then string subscripts sorted by ASCII ("AUTH01", "AUTH02"). The first $ORDER from "" returns 100, the second from 100 returns 200, the third from 200 returns 500. ^errors(500) = "Internal". (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_forder)
